edition.locus: Gebhardt VII.XXI (Saturus's leopard; the kiss of peace; amen)

source_text: Item Saturus in alia porta Pudentem militem exhortabatur dicens: Ad summam, inquit, certe, sicut praesumpsi et praedixi, nullam usque adhuc bestiam sensi. Et nunc de toto corde credas: ecce prodeo illo, et ab uno morsu leopardi consumor. Et statim in fine spectaculi, leopardo eiecto, de uno morsu tanto perfusus est sanguine, ut populus reuertenti illi secundi baptismatis testimonium reclamauerit: Saluum lotum, saluum lotum. Plane utique saluus erat qui hoc modo lauerat. Tunc Pudenti militi: Uale, inquit, memor fidei et mei; et haec te non conturbent, sed confirment. Simulque ansulam de digito eius petiit, et uulneri suo mersam reddidit ei hereditatem, pignus relinquens illi et memoriam sanguinis. Exinde iam exanimis prosternitur cum ceteris ad iugulationem solito loco. Et cum populus illos in medio postularet, ut gladio penetranti in eorum corpore oculos suos comites homicidii adiungerent, ultro surrexerunt et se quo uolebat populus transtulerunt, ante iam osculati inuicem, ut martyrium per solemnia pacis consummarent. Ceteri quidem inmobiles et cum silentio ferrum receperunt: multo magis Saturus, qui et prior ascenderat, prior reddidit spiritum; nam et Perpetuam sustinebat. Perpetua autem, ut aliquid doloris gustaret, inter ossa conpuncta exululauit, et errantem dexteram tirunculi gladiatoris ipsa in iugulum suum transtulit. Fortasse tanta femina aliter non potuisset occidi, quae ab inmundo spiritu timebatur, nisi ipsa uoluisset. O fortissimi ac beatissimi martyres! O uere uocati et electi in gloriam domini nostri Iesu Christi! Quam qui magnificat et honorificat et adorat, utique et haec non minora ueteribus exempla in aedificationem ecclesiae legere debet, ut nouae quoque uirtutes unum et eundem semper spiritum sanctum usque adhuc operari testificentur omnipotentem deum patrem et filium eius Iesum Christum dominum nostrum, cui est claritas et immensa potestas in saecula saeculorum, amen.
pass_a_gloss: Literal gloss: Saturus at another gate was encouraging Pudens the soldier, saying: In sum, he said, surely, just as I presumed and foretold, I have felt no beast yet. And now believe with whole heart: behold I go out to that leopard, and by one bite of a leopard I am consumed. And immediately at the end of the show, with a leopard let out, from one bite he was so covered with blood that the people shouted back to him as he returned the testimony of a second baptism: Saved washed, saved washed. Certainly indeed safe was he who had washed in this way. Then to Pudens the soldier he said: Farewell, remember faith and me; and let these things not disturb you, but strengthen you. And at the same time he asked for a little ring from his finger, and dipped in his wound he gave it back to him as an inheritance, leaving to him a pledge and a remembrance of blood. From that point already lifeless he is laid out with the rest for throat-cutting in the usual place. And when the people demanded them in the middle, so that joining their eyes to the sword penetrating into their body as companions of murder, of their own accord they rose and moved themselves where the people wanted, having already kissed one another before, so that they might complete martyrdom through the solemn rites of peace. The rest indeed motionless and with silence received the iron: much more Saturus, who also had first gone up, first gave up the spirit; for he was also sustaining Perpetua. But Perpetua, so that she might taste something of pain, pierced between bones cried out, and the wandering right hand of the novice gladiator she herself transferred to her own throat. Perhaps so great a woman could not otherwise have been killed, who was feared by the unclean spirit, unless she herself had wished it. O most brave and most blessed martyrs! O truly called and chosen into the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ! Which glory whoever magnifies and honors and adores, assuredly ought to read also these examples not less than the old ones for edification of the church, so that new virtues also may testify that one and the same Holy Spirit even still works, almighty God the Father and his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, to whom is brightness and immense power into ages of ages, amen.
pass_b_english: At another gate Saturus was urging on Pudens the soldier, saying, In short, just as I assumed beforehand and foretold, I have felt no beast at all until now. And now believe with all your heart: look, I go out to that leopard, and by one bite of the leopard I am spent. And at once, at the end of the spectacle, when a leopard was let out, one bite covered him with so much blood that as he came back the people shouted to him the witness of a second baptism: Washed and saved, washed and saved. Surely the one who had washed in this way was saved. Then he said to Pudens the soldier, Farewell, remember the faith and remember me, and let these things not trouble you but strengthen you. At the same time he asked for the little ring from his finger, dipped it in his own wound, and gave it back to him as an inheritance, leaving him a pledge and a remembrance of his blood.

From that moment, already dying, he is laid down with the rest in the usual place for the throat-cutting. And when the crowd demanded them out into the middle, so that their own eyes might join the murder by watching the sword sink into their bodies, they rose willingly and moved to wherever the crowd wished, after first kissing one another, so that they might finish their martyrdom through the solemn rites of peace. The rest received the steel motionless and in silence, and much more Saturus, who had gone up first and first gave up his spirit, for he was also holding up Perpetua. But Perpetua, that she might taste something of pain, cried out when pierced between the bones, and she herself guided the straying right hand of the novice gladiator to her own throat. Perhaps so great a woman, whom the unclean spirit feared, could not have been killed otherwise unless she herself had willed it. O most courageous and most blessed martyrs. O truly called and chosen (Matthew 22:14) into the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ. Whoever magnifies and honors and adores that glory ought surely to read these examples also, no less than the ancient ones, for the building up of the church, so that the new acts of power may likewise testify that one and the same Holy Spirit is still at work, almighty God the Father and his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, to whom is splendor and immeasurable power for ever and ever, amen.

choices.why: genitive secundi baptismatis depends on testimonium, and populus uses it after blood-covering to name martyrdom as baptism in blood

choices.english: Washed and saved, washed and saved
choices.why: accusative masculine exclamations agreeing with understood him returning, joining lotum as washed with saluum as saved

choices.english: through the solemn rites of peace
choices.why: per with accusative gives means, and context is the mutual kiss before death, so pacis is the reconciling kiss
